html:
The Prespa Agreement was signed on 17 June 2018 on the shore of Lake Prespa by the foreign ministers of Greece and Macedonia, settling a 27 year dispute over the country's name.

Macedonia agreed to call itself the Republic of North Macedonia for all purposes, and Greece dropped its veto on its entry into NATO and the European Union. Both sides agreed that the Macedonian language and identity are Slavic and unrelated to the ancient kingdom of Macedon. The deal was unpopular with nationalists in both countries. It took effect in February 2019, and North Macedonia joined NATO in 2020. It ended the dispute that began with the independence vote of 1991.
sum: The Prespa Agreement was signed on 17 June 2018 on the shore of Lake Prespa by the foreign ministers of Greece and Macedonia, settling a 27 year dispute over the country's name.
